sentences.text: An application under Section 389 read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C) has been preferred on behalf of the appellant for suspension of sentence and release on bail during pendency of the appeal in FIR No. 295/2012 under Sections 363/376/343 IPC registered at PS: Safdarjung Enclave.

2. Appellant was convicted vide judgment dated 21.02.2023 and sentenced vide order dated 02.09.2023 to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment (RI) for Seven years with fine of Rs.20,000/- for offence punishable under Section 376 IPC (in default of payment of fine to undergo SI for 06 months); and RI for Two years with fine of Rs. 10,000/- for offence punishable under Section 363 IPC (in default of payment of fine to undergo SI for 03 months); with benefit of Section 428 Cr.P.C.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 15/05/2024 at 01:11:15 3.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant was just above 18 years at the relevant time and both prosecutrix/victim and appellant were closely known to each other.
He further contends that FIR was lodged under pressure of the family members, though prosecutrix/victim had left her home on her own free will.
It is pointed out that appellant has undergone more than half of the sentence and the disposal of appeal is likely to take some time.

sentences.text: Learned APP for the State opposes the application and submits that though the victim had left her place on her own free will, but her consent is immaterial, being a minor.
5. Appellant has undergone custody for a period of 03 years 08 months and 23 days including remission for 01 month 02 days, as per nominal roll on 09.02.2024.
The un-expired portion of sentence is reflected as 03 years 02 months 05 days.

6. Honble Supreme Court in S.L.P. (CRL.) No. 529/2021 titled as "Sonadhar vs. The State of Chhattisgarh", observed as under:
"b) The Delhi High Court Legal Services Committee would take up cases for those convicts who have undergone more than half the sentence in case of fixed term sentences and examine the flexibility of filing a bail application before the High Court."
7. Appellant was just aged about 19 years at the time of commission of offence and victim appears to have left voluntarily.
